wiki_text: On September 15, 2025, Ksi Lisims LNG received a provincial Environmental Assessment Certificate from the British Columbia Environmental Assessment Office and a federal Decision Statement, completing its environmental review under a 'one project, one review' process. On November 13, 2025 the project was referred to the federal Major Projects Office and, alongside LNG Canada Phase 2 and the North Coast Transmission Line, was designated a 'national interest' project. The ~12 mtpa floating LNG project on Pearse Island is a partnership of the Nisga'a Nation, Western LNG (Blackstone-backed; developer and future operator) and Rockies LNG; TotalEnergies holds a stake in Western LNG and 20-year offtake (2 mtpa, alongside Shell at 2 mtpa). As of mid-2026 a final investment decision was still targeted for 2026, with first cargo expected 2028-2029.

LNG Canada loaded its first cargo on June 30, 2025, making Canada an LNG-exporting nation; both Phase 1 trains (combined 14 mtpa) were producing by late 2025. The joint venture (Shell 40%, Petronas 25%, Mitsubishi 15%, PetroChina 15%, KOGAS 5%) is advancing a Phase 2 expansion that would add two trains for a total of ~28 mtpa. A Limited Notice to Proceed for early work was issued to the JGC Fluor BC LNG II joint venture, and a final investment decision on the ~CAD 33 billion Phase 2 is widely expected during 2026; the federal Major Projects Office has designated Phase 2 a 'national interest' project.

Woodfibre LNG (2.1 mtpa, near Squamish BC; Pacific Energy 70%, Enbridge 30%) was roughly 65% complete in late 2025, with all 19 process modules expected on site by spring 2026. Enbridge's project timeline and trade press now target an in-service date of 2027 (revised earlier from 2028). The plant is designed to use electric-drive liquefaction powered by BC Hydro hydroelectricity.
